verses.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he ruled for fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
He did evil in the LORD's eyes. He copied the disgusting practices of the nations the LORD had driven out ahead of the Israelites.
He rebuilt the hilltop shrines his father Hezekiah had torn down. He set up altars for the Baal gods and made Asherah poles. He bowed down to all the stars in the sky and worshiped them.
He built altars in the LORD's temple, the place the LORD had spoken about when he said, "My name will be in Jerusalem forever."
He built altars for all the stars in the sky in both courtyards of the LORD's temple.

He sacrificed his own sons in the fire in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. He practiced magic, fortune telling, and witchcraft, and he went to people who talk with the dead and with spirits. He did much evil in the LORD's eyes and made him angry.

He took the idol he had carved and put it in God's temple. God had said to David and his son Solomon about this temple, "In this temple, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.

I will never again make the Israelites leave the land I gave their ancestors, if only they will be careful to obey everything I have commanded them, all the law, the rules, and the decisions given through Moses."
But Manasseh led the people of Judah and Jerusalem astray, so that they did even more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed ahead of the Israelites.
The LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they did not listen.
So the LORD brought the army commanders of the king of Assyria against them. They captured Manasseh, put a hook in his nose, bound him with bronze chains, and took him to Babylon.
In his trouble, Manasseh begged the LORD his God for help and humbled himself greatly before the God of his ancestors.
When he prayed, the LORD was moved by his prayer and listened to his request. He brought him back to Jerusalem and to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.

After this, Manasseh built an outer wall for the City of David, west of the Gihon spring in the valley, as far as the entrance of the Fish Gate. He built it around the hill of Ophel and made it very high. He also put army commanders in all the walled towns of Judah.
He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the LORD's temple. He also removed all the altars he had built on the temple hill and in Jerusalem, and threw them out of the city.
He rebuilt the LORD's altar and offered peace offerings and thank offerings on it. He told the people of Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
The people still offered sacrifices at the hilltop shrines, but only to the LORD their God.
Everything else Manasseh did, his prayer to his God, and the words the seers spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are written in the records of the kings of Israel.

His prayer and how God answered it, all his sins and unfaithfulness, and the places where he built hilltop shrines and set up Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself, are all written in the records of the seers.
Manasseh died and was buried in his palace. His son Amon became king after him.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he ruled for two years in Jerusalem.
He did evil in the LORD's eyes, just as his father Manasseh had done. Amon offered sacrifices to all the idols his father Manasseh had made, and he worshiped them.
But he did not humble himself before the LORD as his father Manasseh had done. Instead, Amon sinned more and more.
His officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
But the people of the land killed everyone who had plotted against King Amon. Then they made his son Josiah king after him.
